mechanics.name: Ace in the Hole
mechanics.currentEffect: Regular Items retrieved from Chests come with one guaranteed Add-on of Visceral Rarity or lower and a 50/75/100% chance of a second Add-on of Uncommon Rarity or lower. Add-ons on your held Item are retained when you escape.
activation: Retrieve a regular Item from a Chest.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.4.0): Raised the guaranteed Add-on rarity cap to Ultra Rare and increased the tiered second-Add-on chance to 50/75/100%.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Chest Items receive a guaranteed Add-on and may receive a second; their Add-ons are kept on escape.
specialInteractions: Does not add these effects to non-Chest Items.

editorial.summary: Items taken from Chests gain a guaranteed Add-on, may gain a second Add-on, and keep their Add-ons if you escape.
useCases: Improve the expected quality of chest loot.
Pair with Plunderer’s Instinct and Appraisal to generate better-equipped Items.
Escape with valuable Add-ons instead of losing them.
counters: Only regular Items retrieved from Chests receive the Add-ons.
The base Item itself can still be something you do not need.
No immediate match value if you never open a Chest.
pros: Tier III always rolls a second Add-on chance at 100%.
Add-ons can be retained on escape.
cons: No direct chase, repair, healing, or rescue effect.
analysis: Ace in the Hole improves the quality of an activity that is already optional: looting Chests. The perk guarantees one Add-on and can guarantee a second at Tier III, which is meaningful when the Item itself is useful.
Its strongest role is inside a full loot economy. Plunderer’s Instinct finds and accelerates Chests, Appraisal produces more Items, and Ace in the Hole improves what those Items contain.
The weakness is that no amount of Add-on quality makes a badly timed chest detour efficient. The team still needs generators, rescues, and chase time more urgently than random loot in many matches.
That keeps Ace in the Hole low despite solid synergy. It improves chest output rather than solving the fundamental opportunity cost of opening Chests.
editorial.verdict: A good chest-build multiplier and a weak general perk. Better loot is nice; needing loot in the first place is the harder argument.
